min-instances 0 → this service can scale to zero: no instance, no Envoy, no cost. The first call after idle then pays cold start for BOTH containers — the startup probe traverses Envoy → app, so readiness gates on the full path (flow doc §8).
Measured: parallel start, no --depends-on → marginal cost ≈ 0; serialised was a flat +0.65 s.

div.div:
Fleet arithmetic at this instant: 1 client · 1 Apigee instance · 3 services · 9 instances · 18 containers — and therefore 9 Envoy proxies, each holding its own config and its own copy of the JWKS.
Sized as the PoC does (0.25 vCPU / 128 Mi), the sidecar tier costs +2.25 vCPU / +1.1 GiB across the fleet; on per-container defaults (1 vCPU / 512 Mi) the same nine cost +9 vCPU / +4.5 GiB — size the sidecar explicitly.
Nobody deploys nine Envoys: the autoscaler does, per service, and the count moves with load. A config change (JWKS rotation, issuer/audience edit) reaches them only as a new revision on each service — there is no shared control plane, which is the trade against enforcing once at the Apigee edge.
